title: Protein Concentration Determination using Qubit 4 Fluorometer
author: Steven J Burgess
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqnbmvan

steps.title: Prepare Qubit Working Solution
steps.instruction: Create a working solution of Qubit assay buffer by diluting the reagent 1:200 in the provided buffer.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the final volume in each tube is 200 µL.
Prepare sufficient volume to accommodate all standards (190 µL per tube) and samples (180–199 µL per tube).

steps.title: Dilute Protein Samples
steps.instruction: Dilute the protein sample 1:50 to reduce the impact of SDS and 2-mercaptoethanol and to bring the concentration into the linear range (1.25-25 μg/mL).

substeps.instruction: Combine 196 µL dH2O with 4 µL of sample.

steps.title: Prepare Assay Tubes
steps.instruction: Add 190 µL of Qubit working solution to a fresh Qubit assay tube for each sample to be analyzed and for the three protein standards.

steps.title: Add Standards and Samples
steps.instruction: Add the protein standards and diluted samples to their respective tubes and mix.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL of protein standard to the appropriate tube and vortex for 3 seconds.
Add 10 µL of diluted sample to the appropriate tube and vortex for 3 seconds.

steps.title: Incubate Samples
steps.instruction: Allow the samples to incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Measure Protein Concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the protein sample concentration using the Qubit 4 Fluorometer (Invitrogen, Q33238), following the machine's instructions.

substeps.instruction: Start by measuring the standard curve.
Adjust measured values according to the total dilution factor (1:1000, accounting for the 1:50 initial dilution and the 1:20 assay dilution).
